```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
  fig.width = 13, fig.height = 5.5, dpi = 180, fig.retina = 1, out.width = "100%")
source("../../dev/diagnostic_checks/simulation-studies/covariance-pooling/plot.R")
read_results <- function(directory, filename) read.csv(file.path(directory, filename))

conditions <- bind_rows(
  read_results(params$gaussian_directory, "conditions.csv") |> mutate(family = "gaussian"),
  read_results(params$generalized_directory, "conditions.csv"))
# Other families compare methods on the datasets where all of them were available.
summary <- bind_rows(
  read_results(params$gaussian_directory, "summary.csv") |> mutate(family = "gaussian",
    method = recode(method, composition_any = "checks", likelihood_ratio = "comparison",
      pooled_any = "overall")),
  read_results(params$generalized_directory, "summary.csv") |> mutate(method = recode(method,
    composition_paired = "checks", likelihood_ratio_paired = "comparison",
    full_paired = "full", pooled_any = "overall")))
scenario_labels <- c(null = "Correct pooling", variance_small = "SD ratio 1.25",
  variance_large = "SD ratio 1.50", correlation_small = "Correlations 0.10 / 0.30 / 0.50",
  correlation_large = "Correlations -0.10 / 0.30 / 0.70")
summary <- summary |> inner_join(conditions, by = c("family", "condition")) |>
  mutate(scenario = factor(scenario, names(scenario_labels), scenario_labels))
rates <- summary |> filter(allocation == "balanced", method %in% c("checks", "comparison", "full"))
fits <- bind_rows(read_results(params$gaussian_directory, "fits.csv") |> mutate(family = "gaussian"),
  read_results(params$generalized_directory, "fits.csv"))
response_settings <- read_results(params$generalized_directory, "settings.csv")
screening <- read_results(params$generalized_directory, "screening.csv")
nb2_available <- all(file.exists(file.path(params$nb2_directory,
  paste0(c("conditions", "fits", "inference", "selection", "flags"), ".csv"))))

families <- tibble::tribble(
  ~family, ~label,
  "gaussian", "Gaussian",
  "poisson", "Poisson",
  "compois", "COM-Poisson",
  "truncated_poisson", "Zero-truncated Poisson",
  "tweedie", "Tweedie",
  "bell", "Bell",
  "zi_poisson", "Zero-inflated Poisson"
)
percent_range <- function(values) paste0(paste(unique(round(100 * range(values))), collapse = "–"), "%")
correct_pooling <- filter(rates, scenario == "Correct pooling")
small_sample <- rates |> filter(family != "gaussian", method == "checks", n_dyads == min(n_dyads))
figure_descriptions <- as.vector(rbind(
  paste0(families$label, ": detection of incorrect covariance pooling by number of dyads."),
  paste0(families$label, ": false alarms when pooling is correct, by number of dyads.")
))
```

## What these plots compare

Two models allow different means and actor and partner effects for female-female,
female-male, and male-male dyads. The **pooled model** uses one exchangeable
covariance for all dyads. The **full model** estimates a separate covariance for
each composition. We make pooling wrong by changing the female/male SD ratio in
female-male dyads or the partner correlations across compositions. These changes
leave the pooled covariance unchanged. The
[partner-dependence study](partner-dependence-simulation.html) shows how often the
check detects an omitted partner correlation.

- **Orange:** composition checks of the pooled model,
  `check_partner_dependence(role = gender)`. A flag means at least one of 14
  summaries lies outside its middle 95% simulated range.
- **Green:** model comparison of the pooled and full models, a likelihood-ratio
  test at 5% with `compare_nested_models()`.
- **Grey (false-alarm plots of other families):** the same checks of the full
  model, which has the correct structure.

When pooling was correct, composition checks raised false alarms in
`r percent_range(correct_pooling$rate[correct_pooling$method == "checks"])` of
datasets, and model comparison in
`r percent_range(correct_pooling$rate[correct_pooling$method == "comparison"])`.
The checks flagged wrong pooling more often than model comparison in most
settings, partly because of these extra false alarms. Allowing for them, the
checks mostly did better for Gaussian outcomes with up to 200 dyads, and model
comparison usually did better for the other families with 400 dyads. For the
other families with `r min(small_sample$n_dyads)` dyads, the checks flagged `r percent_range(small_sample$rate[small_sample$scenario == "Correct pooling"])`
of correctly pooled datasets, and no more than
`r percent_range(summarise(filter(small_sample, scenario != "Correct pooling"), rate = max(rate), .by = family)$rate)`
of wrongly pooled ones, depending on the family. So a flag or its absence says little.

Use model comparison when both models fit reliably and the comparison is valid.
The checks can reveal mismatches in a simpler model even when the full model
cannot be fitted. Neither a nonsignificant comparison nor an absent flag shows
that the simpler model gives adequate coefficient inference.
Checking all dyads together (`role = NULL`) rarely flagged anything: at most
`r scales::percent(max(summary$rate[summary$method == "overall"], na.rm = TRUE), accuracy = 1)`
in any condition.

<details>
<summary>Study details</summary>

Gaussian outcomes have the covariance on the outcome scale, with residual SDs of 1
and partner correlations of 0.3 under correct pooling. For the other families,
each partner has a Gaussian latent effect on the log scale, with SDs of 0.6 and
correlations of 0.3 under correct pooling. Outcomes are then drawn from the family.
These families passed a
[fitting and recovery screen](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/dev/diagnostic_checks/simulation-studies/generalized-covariance-pooling/screen-families.R)
of `r nrow(screening)` candidates.

Dyads are split roughly equally among the three compositions, so 100 total dyads
means about 33 per composition. Predictors are standard normal, with partner
correlation 0.3. Mean coefficients differ by role and composition, and the mean
model is correct throughout. In practice, omitted predictors can also cause
mismatches.

Checks subtract fitted fixed-effect predictions and use simulations from the
fitted model, without refitting. Failed fits, convergence or Hessian problems,
and unavailable checks are excluded. For the other families, all methods use the
same datasets: those where both checks and the model comparison were available.
The pooled model could be checked in nearly all datasets, but the full model often
had no usable fit with 40 or 100 dyads.

The report uses saved results. See the study code for
[Gaussian outcomes](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/dev/diagnostic_checks/simulation-studies/covariance-pooling/run.R)
and [other families](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/dev/diagnostic_checks/simulation-studies/generalized-covariance-pooling/run.R),
the [plot code](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/dev/diagnostic_checks/simulation-studies/covariance-pooling/plot.R),
and the [study notes](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/dev/diagnostic_checks/simulation-studies/README.md).

</details>

## When the full model is unavailable

The method-comparison plots below use the same datasets for each method. That
paired subset leaves out many failed full fits. This separate reaggregation
retains **all usable simpler-model checks**, including those datasets.

```{r fallback-availability}
fallback_rates <- read_results(params$fallback_directory, "rates.csv")
fallback_totals <- read_results(params$fallback_directory, "totals.csv")
fallback_totals |>
  summarise(Attempted = sum(attempted), Checked = sum(checks_defined),
    `Simpler fit only` = sum(pooled_only), .by = family) |>
  left_join(fallback_rates |> filter(full_fit == "all", scenario == "null") |>
    summarise(`Flags under correct pooling` = percent_range(rate), .by = family),
    by = "family") |>
  mutate(Family = families$label[match(family, families$family)], .before = 1) |>
  select(-family) |> knitr::kable()
```

The last column gives the range across 40, 100 and 400 dyads; it counts any of
14 summaries. These are the original saved quantile flags, not a new validation
of the later rank limits. Full-fit availability here uses the original saved fitting criteria. Failed
simpler fits and unavailable checks remain in the attempted counts, but do not
contribute to flag-rate denominators.

```{r fallback-selection, results='asis'}
example <- fallback_rates |>
  filter(family == "poisson", n_dyads == 100, scenario == "null")
show_rate <- function(group) {
  row <- filter(example, full_fit == group)
  sprintf("%s/%s (%.1f%%; 95%% interval %.1f–%.1f%%)", row$flagged, row$checked,
    100 * row$rate, 100 * row$lower, 100 * row$upper)
}
cat(sprintf("For example, with 100 Poisson dyads and correct pooling, the simpler model flagged in **%s** of datasets where the full fit was unusable, versus **%s** where it was usable. Across both groups the rate was **%s**.\n\n",
  show_rate("unusable"), show_rate("usable"), show_rate("all")))
```

Full-fit failure selects a subset of datasets. Differences between these groups
are therefore descriptive, not effects caused by convergence failure. The saved
records contain no scientific coefficient estimates, so this reaggregation
does not establish whether simplification preserves significance or coverage.

Covariance pooling also does not establish full exchangeability: both fitted
models retain role- and composition-specific means and slopes. An unrestricted
cross-sectional ordinal latent covariance with freely estimated thresholds has a scale
identification problem; these results do not justify fitting that model or
interpreting its failure as evidence for pooling.

```{asis, echo=nb2_available}
## A difficult NB2 fallback case

A separate study uses negative-binomial outcomes with size 3, 100 or 400 dyads,
and correct pooling, a latent SD ratio of 1.5, or correlations of -0.1, 0.3 and
0.7 across compositions. Both fitted models retain the correct role-specific
means and slopes. The female actor effect in female-male dyads is truly zero;
the other three prespecified scientific effects are nonzero.
These are conditional log-link coefficients. With unequal latent variances,
the role-intercept contrast is not the marginal difference in mean outcomes.

We compare always using the pooled model, always using the full model, using the
full model when available with a pooled fallback, and likelihood-ratio selection
at .05. Selection uses the sole usable model if the other fit fails. If neither
fit is usable, or both fit but their comparison is undefined, LRT selection
returns no inference. The known generating effects determine coverage; a usable
full fit is not treated as the truth.
A full fit whose log-likelihood is more than 0.000001 below its usable nested
pooled fit is also excluded: reported convergence alone is insufficient.
Its original numerical status and estimates remain saved.
```

```{r nb2-data, eval=nb2_available, results='asis'}
nb2_conditions <- read_results(params$nb2_directory, "conditions.csv")
nb2_fits <- read_results(params$nb2_directory, "fits.csv") |>
  left_join(nb2_conditions, by = "condition")
nb2_inference <- read_results(params$nb2_directory, "inference.csv") |>
  left_join(nb2_conditions, by = "condition")
nb2_flags <- read_results(params$nb2_directory, "flags.csv") |>
  left_join(nb2_conditions, by = "condition")
nb2_selection <- read_results(params$nb2_directory, "selection.csv") |>
  left_join(nb2_conditions, by = "condition")
nb2_pilot <- any(nb2_conditions$repetitions < 500)
cat(sprintf("The output contains %s fit attempts across six conditions, with %s datasets per condition and %s reference simulations per usable pooled fit.\n\n",
  sum(nb2_fits$attempted), unique(nb2_conditions$repetitions),
  unique(nb2_conditions$reference_draws)))
if (nb2_pilot) cat("**These are pilot results for checking the workflow; they do not establish error rates or justify a fallback recommendation.**\n\n")
nb2_fits |> mutate(Setting = unname(scenario_labels[scenario]),
    Result = paste0(eligible_n, "/", attempted)) |>
  select(Dyads = n_dyads, Setting, model, Result) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = Result) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Eligible fits / attempted fits (including the likelihood check)") |> print()
```

```{asis, echo=nb2_available && !nb2_pilot}
- **Pooling recovered many analyses, but did not ensure accurate inference.**
  The full model was eligible in 1,793/3,000 datasets, the pooled model in
  2,921/3,000, and full-then-pooled fallback returned 2,978/3,000. There were
  1,081 full-model optimizer or Hessian failures and 126 further exclusions for
  worse nested likelihoods. These numerical problems do not alone establish
  structural nonidentifiability.
- **Unequal latent SDs could bias the role contrast.** At 400 dyads and an SD
  ratio of 1.5, pooled-model bias was +0.092 for the true conditional contrast
  of 0.6. Its 95% intervals covered the truth in 89.3% of usable fits (95%
  Monte Carlo interval 86.3–91.8%). Full-then-pooled and LRT selection gave
  94.2% and 92.2% coverage. These use each procedure's available datasets;
  among the same 290 datasets with both models eligible, pooling reduced
  coverage by 8.3 percentage points (95% Monte Carlo interval 4.6–12.0).
- **Quiet diagnostics did not certify a safe fallback.** In that same condition,
  the 207 datasets needing a pooled fallback had 90.3% coverage (85.5–93.7%).
  Dependence, residual and outcome checks flagged only 34.3%, 33.8% and 26.6%
  of this group, respectively. This grouping describes numerical availability;
  it is not a causal comparison or an analysis restricted to unflagged datasets.
- **LRT selection also needs caution.** With correct pooling at 400 dyads,
  the nominal .05 LRT rejected in 50/306 datasets with both fits eligible:
  16.3% (12.6–20.9%). This is conditional on numerical eligibility, not an
  unconditional test-size estimate. The nominal .05 threshold did not yield
  5% rejection in this selected subset.
```

```{asis, echo=nb2_available}
The figure shows false positives for the true-zero female actor effect, using
all returned usable estimates. Error bars are 95% Wilson intervals. Returned
```

```{r nb2-null, eval=nb2_available, fig.height=5.5, fig.alt="False positives for a true-zero female actor effect under four model-choice procedures, by sample size and covariance restriction."}
nb2_methods <- c(policy_pooled = "Pooled", policy_full = "Full",
  policy_full_then_pooled = "Full, then pooled", policy_lrt_05 = "LRT .05")
nb2_inference |>
  filter(parameter == "female_actor_null", method %in% names(nb2_methods)) |>
  mutate(Rule = factor(method, names(nb2_methods), nb2_methods),
    Setting = factor(scenario, c("null", "variance_large", "correlation_large"),
      c("Correct pooling", "SD ratio 1.5", "Correlations -0.1 / 0.3 / 0.7")),
    Dyads = paste(n_dyads, "dyads")) |>
  ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(rejection, Rule, colour = Rule)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = .05, linetype = 2, colour = "grey55") +
  ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(xmin = rejection_lower, xmax = rejection_upper),
    orientation = "y", width = .15) + ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(Dyads ~ Setting) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = c("#D55E00", "#333333", "#009E73", "#0072B2")) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Null effects declared significant", y = NULL,
    caption = if (nb2_pilot) "Pilot only: these rates do not establish calibration." else NULL) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 11) + ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{asis, echo=nb2_available}
Pooled-model diagnostics below use the same reference bank for dependence,
residual and outcome checks. Each rate counts any panel within that check;
these unions do not have a joint 5% error rate. The saved tables also separate
individual panels and datasets with eligible or ineligible full fits.
```

```{r nb2-diagnostics, eval=nb2_available}
nb2_flags |> filter(scope == "union", full_fit == "all") |>
  mutate(Setting = unname(scenario_labels[scenario]),
    Result = sprintf("%s/%s (%.1f%%)", flagged_n, checked, 100 * rate)) |>
  select(Dyads = n_dyads, Setting, check, Result) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = check, values_from = Result) |> knitr::kable()
```

```{asis, echo=nb2_available}
<details>
<summary>Inference for all four scientific targets</summary>

These summaries use every returned usable estimate from each procedure, without conditioning on
the presence or absence of a flag. Coverage and rejection percentages use the
returned estimates as their denominator. The saved policy tables retain every
attempt and its selected model, including cases with no inference.
```

```{r nb2-inference, eval=nb2_available}
nb2_inference |> filter(primary, grepl("^policy_", method)) |>
  mutate(Setting = unname(scenario_labels[scenario])) |>
  arrange(n_dyads, scenario, parameter, method) |>
  transmute(Dyads = n_dyads, Setting, Target = parameter,
    Rule = sub("policy_", "", method), Available = paste(available_n, attempted, sep = "/"),
    Bias = round(bias, 3), `SE ratio` = round(se_ratio, 2),
    `Coverage (%)` = round(100 * coverage, 1), `Rejection (%)` = round(100 * rejection, 1)) |>
```

```{asis, echo=nb2_available && file.exists(file.path(params$nb2_directory, "paired-inference.csv"))}
<details>
<summary>Paired sensitivity: coverage changes relative to the full model</summary>

These secondary comparisons use only datasets where both models were eligible.
They describe a selected subset, not the datasets requiring fallback. Changes
are percentage points; brackets show approximate 95% Monte Carlo intervals
using paired per-dataset differences. Full-then-pooled equals full in this subset.
```

```{asis, echo=nb2_available}
This is a bounded check of one difficult count family. It does not validate
unidentified ordinal structures, full exchangeability of means and slopes, or
selection over many alternative role definitions. An absent flag still does not
establish that the simpler model gives adequate inference.
```

```{r family-results, results='asis', fig.alt=figure_descriptions}
for (family_index in seq_len(nrow(families))) {
  family_name <- families$family[family_index]
  family_label <- families$label[family_index]
  gaussian <- family_name == "gaussian"
  family_conditions <- filter(conditions, family == family_name)
  family_rates <- filter(rates, family == family_name)
  plot_arguments <- list(family_label = family_label,
    subtitle = if (gaussian) "outcomes, residual covariance" else
      "outcomes, latent covariance on the log scale",
    repetitions = unique(family_conditions$repetitions),
    reference_draws = unique(family_conditions$reference_draws), same_datasets = !gaussian)
  cat("\n\n## ", family_label, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(do.call(plot_pooling_detection, c(list(
    filter(family_rates, scenario != "Correct pooling", method != "full")), plot_arguments)))
  print(do.call(plot_pooling_false_alarms, c(list(
    filter(family_rates, scenario == "Correct pooling")), plot_arguments)))

  cat("<details>\n<summary>Model settings and checks</summary>\n\n")
  family_fits <- filter(fits, family == family_name)
  if (gaussian) {
    cat("All ", format(sum(family_fits$attempted), big.mark = ","), " fits were usable. The table also counts flags on a summary that truly differed, ",
      "in the expected direction, and results with unequal group sizes (20 female-female, ",
      "60 female-male, and 20 male-male dyads).\n\n", sep = "")
    summary |> filter(family == "gaussian", scenario != "Correct pooling",
        (allocation == "balanced" & n_dyads %in% c(100, 400)) | allocation == "unbalanced",
        method %in% c("checks", "expected_direction", "comparison")) |>
      mutate(dyads = ifelse(allocation == "unbalanced", "100 (20 / 60 / 20)", as.character(n_dyads)),
        percentage = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * rate)) |>
      select(scenario, dyads, method, percentage) |>
      tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = percentage) |>
      arrange(scenario, dyads) |>
      select(scenario, dyads, checks, expected_direction, comparison) |>
      knitr::kable(col.names = c("Setting", "Dyads", "Any flag", "Flag in expected direction",
        "Model comparison")) |> print()
  } else {
    settings <- filter(response_settings, family == family_name)
    cat("**Response:** ", settings$response_settings, "; log link.\n\n", sep = "")
    available <- family_rates |> filter(method == "checks") |>
      summarise(range = paste(unique(range(checked)), collapse = "–"), .by = n_dyads)
    cat("**Datasets with all methods available:** ",
      paste0(available$range, " of ", unique(family_conditions$repetitions), " at ",
        available$n_dyads, " dyads", collapse = "; "), ".\n\n", sep = "")
    if (family_name == "compois") cat("Simulations failed for ", sum(family_fits$check_failures),
      " fitted models (sampler overflow or non-finite draws).\n\n", sep = "")
    if (family_name == "tweedie") cat("Simulations used an equivalent, faster sampler ",
      "([details](https://github.com/Pascal-Kueng/dyadMLM/blob/main/dev/diagnostic_checks/simulation-studies/README.md#tweedie-simulation-repair)).\n\n", sep = "")
    if (family_name == "zi_poisson") cat("Both models estimate a zero-inflation ",
      "intercept without random effects.\n\n", sep = "")
    unavailable <- sum(family_fits$comparison_failures)
    if (unavailable > 0) cat("Model comparison was unavailable for ", unavailable,
      if (unavailable == 1) " dataset" else " datasets",
      " because the full model had a lower log-likelihood than the pooled model.\n\n", sep = "")
  }
  cat("\n\n</details>\n\n")
}
```
